questions.question: You’re waiting in line at the café when someone cuts ahead of you. How would you politely respond if they apologise?
options: That’s not fair! I was right behind you!
Oh, no, it’s fine. It happens all the time.
I’m sorry for waiting so long—you should have gone first.
Don’t worry about it; I’ll just wait my turn.
questions.answer: Oh, no, it’s fine. It happens all the time.

questions.question: Your friend suggests going to a local market on Sunday, but you’re busy. What would be the most appropriate way to respond?
options: Yes, that sounds great! I’ll definitely go with you.
I’m afraid I can’t make it this time, but thanks for asking.
Why not? It’s a good idea, but I’ll have to think about it.
I don’t like markets anyway; they’re too crowded.
questions.answer: I’m afraid I can’t make it this time, but thanks for asking.

questions.question: A colleague asks if you’d like to join them for lunch after work. What would be the most polite way to decline?
options: No, thanks—I’ve got plans for the afternoon.
I’d love to, but I’m already booked with someone else.
I don’t eat lunch with colleagues; it’s too informal.
I’m sorry, but I can’t. I have a meeting at 12:30.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, but I can’t. I have a meeting at 12:30.

questions.question: You’re in a formal meeting and someone asks if you’d like to contribute your opinion. How would you respond appropriately?
options: No, I don’t think I have anything to add.
That’s a great question! I’d love to share my thoughts.
I’m not sure if I’m qualified to say anything on this topic.
I’ll keep that in mind, but I’ll have to think about it first.
questions.answer: That’s a great question! I’d love to share my thoughts.

questions.question: Your partner offers to help you move some furniture, but you’re already prepared. What would be the most appropriate way to respond?
options: Thanks, but I’ve got this under control. You don’t need to bother.
That’s really kind of you, but I’m good—I don’t need help.
I don’t want to impose, but I’d be grateful if you could help me.
No, that’s not necessary; I’ll do it myself.
questions.answer: That’s really kind of you, but I’m good—I don’t need help.
